title: Lunar: Eternal Blue
subtitle: A visitor from the Blue Star
summary: Lunar: Eternal Blue is Game Arts and Studio Alex's role-playing sequel, first released for Mega-CD in Japan on 22 December 1994.
body: Lunar: Eternal Blue is Game Arts and Studio Alex's role-playing sequel, first released for Mega-CD in Japan on 22 December 1994. A thousand years after The Silver Star, the explorer Hiro meets Lucia, a visitor from the distant Blue Star seeking to prevent a catastrophe. Their journey gathers companions and brings them into conflict with Zophar. Towns, dungeons and turn-based encounters again provide the structure, while more elaborate animation and extensive spoken dialogue make fuller use of the disc hardware to present the cast and its changing relationships.

Combat builds on the original's use of distance, requiring characters to approach a target or attack from range. The player can arrange the party's starting positions, giving a chance to prepare for the next exchange before commands are carried out. Experience improves the characters' strength, while separate magical progression expands their abilities. The arrangement connects preparation to the visible action: choosing where a companion begins can influence how quickly that fighter reaches an enemy, and the party's growing repertoire offers more answers to the creatures encountered along the route.

Noriyuki Iwadare's music supports a world that carries the earlier adventure as history, allowing the sequel to revisit familiar ideas through another generation of characters. Working Designs' North American release followed in September 1995, with a localised script that emphasised the companions' personalities and humour. Later remakes changed the presentation again, but the original already pushed the Mega-CD's storytelling ambitions further. Its combination of longer animated sequences, voices and party-based encounters gave Hiro and Lucia's journey a sense of continuity between the scenes watched and the decisions made during exploration.
